author: evac
description: Mirrors the photos and videos of a Telegram forum group you belong to into Discord, one channel per Telegram topic you choose to map, one at a time. Media only: no text, captions, usernames or file names ever reach Discord. Reads through your own Telegram user session (Telethon), strictly read-only and heavily throttled (jittered polling, spaced downloads, hourly and daily caps, automatic pause on Telegram flood limits). Videos are downloaded to a temp folder, over-limit clips are shrunk with ffmpeg, then everything is posted and the temp files are deleted. Albums stay together. A mod-only X under every post removes it and logs the removal to the mod log.
install_msg:
Thanks for installing tgfeed!

One-time setup:
1. Get an api_id / api_hash at my.telegram.org -> API development tools. Put them in the red service's environment in docker-compose.yml as TG_API_ID and TG_API_HASH, then recreate the container (`docker compose up -d`). Never paste them in Discord.
2. Log in once, in a terminal on the host: `docker exec -it red python /data/cogs/CogManager/cogs/tgfeed/login.py` (phone number, the code Telegram sends you, your 2FA password if set).
3. In Discord: `.tgfeed group <invite link of the group you are in>`, then `.tgfeed category <category>`, `.tgfeed topics`, then `.tgfeed map <topic>` for each topic you want (creates a channel visible only to you; or `.tgfeed map <topic> #channel` for an existing one).

Only new posts are mirrored; there is no backfill. `.tgfeed status` shows the caps and the last cycle.
name: TGFeed
short: Telegram forum group photos/videos -> Discord channels, media only, read-only and throttled.
end_user_data_statement: This cog stores no end-user data. It stores guild-level configuration (the Telegram group, topic-to-channel mappings, throttle settings), and a Telegram session file on the host. No message text, usernames or captions are read into storage.
